I'm writing these from prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 and haven't run any queries. No tools were used. Rough confidence is in brackets.

- **Replacing `none` with a real op (edges 0-5).** Such an edit gains more than replacing any other op, because it restores connectivity and capacity. This should hold across all three datasets and an intuitive reader would agree. [0.8-0.9]
- **Removing a conv3x3 edge.** Removal hurts more than removing a weaker op. [0.8]
- **Dead-node effects.** If edge 0 is `none`, node 1 is disconnected, so edits to edges 2 and 4 matter less. Edit effects on edge 1 matter more. [0.6-0.7]
- **Saturation.** Adding a conv when strong ops already exist elsewhere gives less gain. [0.5-0.6]
